nodes.description: Reflux is reported particularly in infants and young children.

evidence.snippet: Frequent vomiting and gastroesophageal reflux disease have been reported occasionally in newborns and small children.

nodes.description: Gastrointestinal manifestations include constipation, reflux, feeding difficulties and occasional structural anomalies, with different mechanisms and management needs.

evidence.snippet: Gastrointestinal dysfunction (41%) ... Frequent chronic constipation (requiring daily medication) & reflux disease

nodes.description: Developmental delay varies markedly. Motor and language development may be delayed even when no cortical malformation is visible on imaging.

evidence.snippet: Developmental delay (DD) / intellectual disability (ID) is highly variable: ... In children with normal brain structure, motor delay is common

nodes.description: Hearing aids may improve access to sound; device selection and follow-up depend on audiologic findings.

evidence.snippet: Hearing aids may be helpful; per otolaryngologist.

nodes.description: A highly arched palate is described in the clinical cohort.

nodes.description: Highly arched eyebrows are a characteristic facial feature.

evidence.snippet: Bilateral ptosis (90%) ... Highly arched eyebrows (90%)

nodes.description: A horseshoe kidney is one reported form of structural renal involvement.

evidence.snippet: Genitourinary abnormalities can include hydronephrosis, horseshoe or ectopic kidneys, renal duplication, and hypospadias.

nodes.description: Dilatation of the renal collecting system is reported in approximately one quarter of affected individuals.

evidence.snippet: Hydronephrosis (23%) ... Structural renal malformation (10%)

nodes.description: Widely spaced eyes are a highly frequent craniofacial manifestation.

evidence.snippet: Widely spaced eyes (95%) ... Bilateral ptosis (90%)

nodes.description: Hypospadias is a rare reported genital manifestation.

evidence.snippet: Genitourinary abnormality (41%) ... Micropenis, cryptorchidism, & hypospadias (rare)

nodes.description: Muscular hypotonia is variable and can particularly affect the upper body.

evidence.snippet: Variable muscular hypotonia, particularly of the upper body, is frequent

nodes.description: Overexpressed ACTB Ser348Leu has reduced localization at epithelial cell junctions in MDCK cells and live Xenopus animal-cap epithelium. Diffuse mutant protein does not behave like endogenous filamentous actin during latrunculin treatment. Impaired incorporation is favored, but detailed polymerization effects remain unresolved.

animal_models.name: ACTB Ser348Leu Overexpression in Xenopus Embryos

evidence.snippet: In contrast, the mutant ACTB (p.S348L) did not show an intense signal at the cell junction but rather showed uniform expression in the cytoplasm

nodes.description: Intellectual disability ranges from mild to profound. Structural brain abnormalities influence severity, but impairment also occurs with apparently normal brain structure; rare individuals have normal intelligence.

evidence.snippet: In children with normal brain structure, motor delay is common, but otherwise development is only mildly to moderately delayed. ID is usually mild. Rare individuals with normal intelligence have also been reported.

nodes.description: Malrotation is a rare structural gastrointestinal manifestation.

evidence.snippet: Structural malformations include duodenal atresia and intestinal malrotation

nodes.description: Unilateral or bilateral iris coloboma may occur, sometimes extending into the posterior segment. The roughly 30% frequency for all ocular coloboma is not an iris-specific estimate.

evidence.snippet: Uni- or bilateral ocular coloboma that may extend from the iris to the macula, sometimes with microphthalmia

nodes.description: Kyphosis contributes to the characteristic stance in some teenagers and adults.

evidence.snippet: Many affected individuals, especially teenagers and adults, have a peculiar stance with kyphosis

nodes.description: Severe lissencephaly is less frequent than pachygyria and can accompany profound developmental impairment.

evidence.snippet: Frontal or predominantly central pachygyria; more rarely, severe lissencephaly or microlissencephaly

nodes.description: Long palpebral fissures are common; their length is distinct from the downslanting orientation that may accompany them.

evidence.snippet: Long, often downslanted palpebral fissures (with or without epicanthal folds or epicanthus inversus)

nodes.description: The philtrum is often long.

evidence.snippet: Long and smooth philtrum and thin vermilion border of the upper lip

nodes.description: Lower-limb spasticity was reported in seven of 21 assessed ACTB cases in the 2015 table; ACTG1 status was not available. These selected-cohort counts are not a general gene-specific penetrance estimate.

evidence.snippet: Spasticity of lower limbs ... 7 ... 14

nodes.description: Microcephaly may be prenatal or develop postnatally. Severity varies, with severe cases accompanying lissencephaly; it is not exclusively a secondary postnatal process.

evidence.snippet: Microcephaly (~50%) Microcephaly may be of prenatal onset, usually mild, but may be severe w/lissencephaly

nodes.description: Microphthalmia can accompany ocular coloboma.

nodes.description: Osmotic laxatives are used for constipation, with gastrointestinal review of long-term medication.

evidence.snippet: Osmotic laxatives were reported effective in majority of persons w/constipation.

nodes.description: Pachygyria is often anterior predominant. The 2015 clinically ascertained cohort reported it in nearly all ACTG1 cases and approximately 60% of ACTB cases; these selected-cohort proportions should not be treated as invariant gene-specific penetrance.

evidence.reference_title: Baraitser-Winter cerebrofrontofacial syndrome: delineation of the spectrum in 42 cases.
evidence.snippet: Nearly all patients with ACTG1 mutations, and around 60% of those with ACTB mutations have some degree of pachygyria with anteroposterior severity gradient, rarely lissencephaly or neuronal heterotopia.

nodes.description: Persistence of the ductus arteriosus is reported.

evidence.snippet: Cardiovascular malformations such as patent ductus arteriosus, ventricular or atrial septal defects

nodes.description: Patient organoids were compared with SC102A-1 and CRTDi011-A control lines. Mutant organoids were smaller, with altered apical progenitor cleavage orientation and reduced ventricular-zone progenitor abundance. Cytoskeletal abnormalities were observed, but their causal relation to altered division orientation was not established. No patient-variant correction or direct cell-fate tracing was reported.

evidence.reference_title: Cerebral organoids expressing mutant actin genes reveal cellular mechanism underlying microcephaly.
evidence.snippet: We generated cerebral organoids from two clones of each patient-derived iPSC line.

nodes.description: The founding study tested actin protein abundance, F-actin organization, morphology, and latrunculin A response. ACTB Arg196His and ACTG1 Ser155Phe cells showed increased F-actin but opposite drug responses; actin protein abundance was unchanged. These non-neural cells do not directly establish cortical developmental mechanisms.

evidence.reference_title: De novo mutations in the actin genes ACTB and ACTG1 cause Baraitser-Winter syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Epstein-Barr virus immortalized lymphoblastoid cell lines were established from peripheral blood samples of six affected individuals (LR04-173, LP98-096, LR09-079, LP98-085, LR04-298 and LR06-241) and two control individuals (09.1359 and 07.0841) using standard procedures.

evidence.reference_title: De novo mutations in the actin genes ACTB and ACTG1 cause Baraitser-Winter syndrome.

nodes.description: ACTB Ser348Leu shows reduced association with exogenous PFN1 in GFP-pulldown experiments from transfected MDCK cells. This allele-specific result suggests altered interactions with an actin-polymerization factor; an equilibrium affinity constant was not measured.

evidence.snippet: We detected similar expression levels between the mutant (p.S348L) ... while the signal of PFN1 was noticeably reduced in the sample with mutant ACTB (p.S348L)

nodes.description: MDCK cells overexpressing ACTB Ser348Leu close a defined cell-free gap more slowly than cells overexpressing wild-type ACTB. This experimental behavior supports a candidate epithelial contribution to clefting rather than a directly observed patient palatal-fusion defect.

evidence.snippet: We observed that the mutant ACTB (p.S348L) -overexpressing cells displayed slower migration over time than the wild-type ACTB-overexpressing cells

nodes.description: The organoid ventricular zone contains fewer progenitors per ventricle-like structure and is thinner. The basal-progenitor-to-radial-glia ratio is increased; greater basal progenitor production is inferred from these observations. Apoptotic cells remain rare and the proportions of Ki-67- and PH3-positive cells are not significantly different, so progenitor depletion should not be equated with a general cell-cycle arrest.

evidence.reference_title: Cerebral organoids expressing mutant actin genes reveal cellular mechanism underlying microcephaly.
evidence.snippet: quantification of the DAPI-stained nuclei revealed a substantial decrease of the number of VZ progenitors per ventricle-like structure in the BWCFF-S organoids as compared to control organoids

nodes.description: In a child with ACTG1 Gly168Cys, glasses and occlusion therapy improved visual acuity from 20/100 right and 20/50 left to 25/25 in both eyes over three years. The maculae were spared by the colobomata, limiting generalization to other ocular anatomy.

evidence.reference_title: Ocular findings in Baraitser-Winter syndrome with a de novo mutation in the ACTG1 gene: a case report.
evidence.snippet: For amblyopia treatment, glasses were prescribed for full correction, and occlusion therapy was started for the left eye. After 3 years of regular follow-up after the initial diagnosis, the patient’s visual acuity had improved to 25/25 in both eyes.

nodes.description: Structural renal anomalies include horseshoe or ectopic kidneys and duplication. Hydronephrosis is recorded separately.

nodes.description: Scoliosis may progress with neuromuscular involvement.

evidence.snippet: progressive, generalized muscle weakness. Some adults may become dependent on a wheelchair for mobility and develop late-onset spinal deformity (kyphosis, scoliosis).

nodes.description: Epilepsy affects approximately half of reported individuals and varies in type and severity. Onset is age dependent, ranging from the first months of life into adulthood. Some seizures are difficult to control, but refractoriness is not universal.

evidence.snippet: Epilepsy, of no specific type and of variable severity, is present in 50% of individuals, often in conjunction with structural cerebral anomalies.

nodes.description: Sensorineural hearing impairment may be progressive and require amplification. Conductive hearing loss also occurs, so the combined 35% hearing-loss frequency is not applied to this subtype.

The model perturbs actin function but does not recreate a heterozygous human missense allele; epithelial migration and PFN1 binding were not measured in these crispants.
